analyst_view.overall: Besiktas (8th, 7 points) host Hapoel Be'er Sheva (33rd, 1 point) in Batumi, Georgia, because UEFA moved the game out of Istanbul for security reasons; most of the crowd is expected to be Besiktas fans, so it should still feel close to a home game. Vincenzo Italiano is expected to make about four changes from the 4-2 win at Konyaspor (Ouattara, Emirhan Topcu, Orkun Kokcu and Cerny in, per TRT Spor via NTV Spor), and one Turkish report says he wants to limit Vlahovic's and Trossard's minutes with the Galatasaray derby next. Hapoel are without first-choice keeper Ofir Marciano, Lucas Ventura and Dan Biton, with Eliel Peretz a big doubt; the numbers already count all of these. Danish referee Morten Krogh shows few cards (2.9 a game), which the numbers already take off. The only new point is Besiktas managing their stars' minutes, so I go a touch lower on goals and shots on target.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, 2.3 for Besiktas, and already lift Besiktas for 15 goals in their last 6 (+4.1%) and for Marciano missing in Hapoel's goal (+6.2%). They cannot see that Italiano reportedly plans to keep Vlahovic's and Trossard's minutes down before the Galatasaray derby, with Kokcu and Cerny rotating in, so I trim mildly to about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 7.3 corners, 4.7 for Besiktas, already trimmed slightly for both sides' recent corner counts. Besiktas should have most of the ball against a side near the bottom, and the neutral venue and the rotation change faces more than how often they reach the byline, so I stay at about 7.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, with Hapoel the more booked side, and already take 12% off for referee Morten Krogh's low card rate (2.9 a game). The political background brings heavy security, but with a mostly Besiktas crowd and a side expected to dominate, nothing points clearly up or down, so I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.0 shots, 19.0 for Besiktas, already nudged for recent form. Even with Vlahovic and Trossard possibly coming off early, Besiktas' changed attack (Cerny, Olaitan, Oh) should keep shooting often against a weak defence, so I stay at about 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 on target, 7.7 for Besiktas, already lifted for sharp recent finishing (+3.9%) and trimmed for Hapoel (-5.9%). Fewer minutes for Vlahovic and Trossard, Besiktas' best finishers, take a little off the quality of their shots, so I go slightly lower, to about 10.2.
